question: What will the Northern Sierra 8-Station Precipitation Index be for November 26, 2026 (water-year-to-date, inches)?

calls.reasoning: 8SI is at 3.44 in WYTD on 11/16 per CDEC (11/16 row may be partial). The forecast strongest-of-season storm Nov 17-20 calls for 2-4 in of mountain liquid (NWS/Yubanet); the weekend storms added ~2.7 to the index, so this one plausibly adds ~3.5 (2.5-5). Nov 21-26 is low-confidence: a possible break, then NWS flags a heavy-precip risk Nov 25-27 and CPC favours wet, so ~0-3 more counts by 11/26. Median ~8.3 in. No human market found (Polymarket/Kalshi/Manifold searched).
calls.dossier:
- CDEC 8SI daily (fetched 2026-11-16 ~08:40 PST): RAIN WYTD 0.46 (10/23), 0.71 (11/04-11/12), 0.72 (11/13), 2.15 (11/14, +1.43), 2.22 (11/15, +0.07), 3.44 (11/16, +1.22). The 11/16 row was already posted early in the day, so it may be partial; KCRA says snow continued in the Sierra into Monday 11/16 afternoon.
- Yubanet/NWS Sacramento AFD summary (Nov 15): the mid-week storm runs Tue night Nov 17 through Thu Nov 19, with lingering showers Fri Nov 20. Mountains get 2-4 in of rain/liquid, with 1-3 ft of snow above 6,000 ft. There is 'increasing potential for active weather to continue next weekend into Thanksgiving Week.'
- Watchers.news (Nov 16): two ARs. NWS Sacramento expects 1-2 ft of snow above 5,000 ft in the northern Sierra and southern Cascades, and travel very difficult to impossible Tue night through early Fri Nov 20. It gives no amounts for after Nov 20.
- KCRA/search summary (Nov 16): the midweek system could be the strongest of the season. Northern California could get 3-5 in of rain. Model probability of 12+ in of snow above 5,000 ft is 70-100%, and of 2 ft is 40-70%.
- Country Herald / NOAA (Nov 15): Thanksgiving-week (Nov 22-28) mountain snow is possible but there are no accumulation totals and confidence is low. A separate search summary cites NWS: higher risk of heavy precipitation and strong winds Nov 25-27, with a possible brief break the weekend of Nov 21-22.
- CPC 8-14 day outlook favours above-average precipitation over much of California for Nov 21 - Dec 4 (per question background).
- For scale: the weekend storms (Nov 13-16), forecast at 1-3 in of mountain liquid, raised the index by ~2.7 in. Past November monthly totals: 13.49 (Nov 2024), 7.72 (Nov 2025).
- Status quo / current level: 3.44 in. The index cannot fall, so the outcome is at least ~3.44.
- Resolves off the first-published CDEC 8SI RAIN value on the row dated 11/26/2026, not off the individual stations or later revisions.
- Event window: accumulation through the CDEC row dated 11/26/2026. As of Now (11/16) about 10 daily rows remain (11/17-11/26), plus any upward revision of the possibly partial 11/16 row.
- Searched but not found: a WPC 7-day QPF for 8SI stations specifically, and any prediction market (none on Polymarket/Kalshi/Manifold).
calls.reference_class: 8SI index gains over 10-day windows that include a forecast strong atmospheric river in an active November pattern (e.g. Nov 2024 ~13 in for the month, Nov 2025 7.7 in for the month)

calls.reasoning: CDEC 8SI shows 3.44 in WYTD on 11/16 after 1.43 (11/14) and 1.22 (11/16). NWS STO AFD (Nov 16 AM) forecasts 2-3.5 in liquid in the mountains for the Tue-Fri storm, plus residual Monday precip, and an active pattern returning for the weekend into Thanksgiving week. Adding ~0.5 (Mon remainder) + ~2.5 (midweek AR) + ~1.5 (weekend-Nov 26) to 3.44 gives a ~7.7 median. Right skew comes from possible additional ARs; the floor is the current value plus a near-certain midweek storm. No human market found (Polymarket/Manifold none per harness; no Kalshi/bookmaker contract found).

calls.reasoning: CDEC shows 8SI at 3.44 in through the 11/16 row (1.43 on 11/14, 0.07 on 11/15, 1.22 on 11/16; 11/16 possibly still partial). NWS Sacramento (11/16 AFD) gives 1.5-2.75in liquid in the foothills and 1-3ft of snow in the mountains for the Tue night-Fri storm, with amounts trending up; Yubanet and AccuWeather give 2-4in for the mountains. That storm should add ~2-4in to the 8-station average. The 'active pattern' NWS mentions for the weekend into Thanksgiving week adds 0-4in, but Swain notes a possible drier break in late November. Median ~7.8in. No market found on Polymarket, Kalshi, Manifold or bookmakers.
calls.dossier:
- CDEC 8SI daily (fetched 2026-11-16 ~16:40Z): WYTD 0.71 through 11/12; 11/13 +0.01 (0.72); 11/14 +1.43 (2.15); 11/15 +0.07 (2.22); 11/16 +1.22 (3.44). The 11/16 row may be partial or still being revised at fetch time.
- October total about 0.47in (0.21 on 10/22, 0.24 on 10/23).
- NWS Sacramento AFD, 348 AM PST Mon Nov 16: Winter Storm Watch Tue evening through early Fri. Liquid totals 1.50-2.75in for the foothills and 1.25-2in for the Valley; 1-2ft of snow above 5000ft, up to 3ft on peaks. Latest trend raised amounts from I-80 south. Mentions an 'active pattern returning for the weekend' and 'potential to continue into Thanksgiving week'; no amounts given for that.
- Yubanet (Nov 15, citing NWS): Sun-Mon system 0.25-1.5in at lower elevations; midweek storm 2-4in in mountains and foothills, 1-3ft of snow above 6000ft; possibly active into Thanksgiving week.
- AccuWeather via Yahoo (Nov 16): 2-4in of rain for northern and central CA through Friday (another source cited 3-5in); 2-3ft of snow above 7000ft; Monday storm quick-hitting, second storm Wed-Thu is bigger.
- Weather West (Swain, Nov 11): 3-4 successive storms over about 9 days (roughly Nov 13-20); all GEFS members give SF at least 1in, most more than 3in. Possible drier/warmer break later in November into early December. Extreme El Nino; record warm coastal SSTs.
- Holiday outlooks (Fox/Yahoo): rain early in Thanksgiving week from NorCal northward; no single big storm signalled for Thanksgiving Day itself.
- 8SI stations (Shasta Dam, Blue Canyon, Pacific House are wet; Sierraville, Mt Shasta City are drier) are averaged, so the index typically runs between foothill and high-mountain point totals.
- Status quo: the index can't fall; the floor is about 3.44 plus whatever falls later on 11/16.
- Resolution: resolves off the CDEC QueryDaily 8SI RAIN column, row 11/26/2026, first published value. Rain falling after the 11/26 label's cutoff doesn't count.
- Event window: accumulation counts through the 11/26 label. As of Now (11/16) about 10 days remain, and the WY-to-date value is banked from 10/1.
- Searched but not found: CNRFC 8SI-specific QPF; WPC 7-day amounts for Nov 21-26; any prediction market (none on Polymarket, Manifold, or Kalshi).
calls.reference_class: Banked WYTD value plus NWS/WPC-style QPF for forecast storm systems over a 10-day window in an active wet-season pattern

calls.reasoning: 8SI at 3.44 in WYTD on the 11/16 row (possibly partial). Rest of Monday's system adds ~0.3-0.8. The Tue-Fri storm is forecast at 2-3.5 (NWS) to 2-4 in (Yubanet/AccuWeather) mountain liquid; last weekend's storms ran near the top of their forecast (+2.7), so I expect ~3 in (2-4.5) to the index. Nov 21-26 is low-confidence: NWS says active weekend pattern and heavy-precip risk ~Nov 25-27, CPC wet, Swain flags a possible break; ~1.2 in median. Median ~8.1, right skew. No human market found.
calls.reconciliation: The runs agree on the CDEC values (3.44 through the 11/16 row, possibly partial), on the NWS midweek QPF (2-3.5 in mountains; 1.5-2.75 in foothills; other outlets 2-4 in), and that no market exists. NWS and Yubanet/AccuWeather ranges overlap, so the midweek totals are not in factual conflict. The remaining differences are judgment: how much of the mountain QPF shows up in the 8-station average, and how much the low-confidence Nov 21-26 period adds. The weekend storms ran near the top of their forecast, which supports ~3 in midweek. Part of any Nov 25-27 event would fall after the 11/26 cutoff, which tempers the late-period amount. I land at median 8.1, slightly above Runs 2/3 and below Run 1, on the component sum rather than by averaging. I carry forward a dispersion of about 5.6. No web retrieval on this run.
